context.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a hybrid cloud Modern Claims Platform that gradually replaces a legacy COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims system over a 3-year period. Its core purpose is to enable online claim submission and adjuster workflows while maintaining strict data consistency and synchronization with the mainframe.

## Key Elements
- Customers and Brokers (External Actors)
- Claims Adjusters (Internal Actors)
- Modern Claims Platform (System-of-Interest, Azure-hosted)
- Legacy Mainframe (External System of Record, COBOL/DB2, on-premise)
- Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL) (Container within Modern Claims Platform)
- Active Directory / Azure AD (External Identity Provider)
- Azure Service Bus and Azure Logic Apps (Integration Containers)
- Notification Service, Payment Gateway, Document Management System, Audit & Compliance System (External Systems)

## Relationships
- Customers/Brokers to Modern Claims Platform via HTTPS (REST/JSON)
- Adjusters to Modern Claims Platform via HTTPS (REST/JSON) for sub-2s response times
- Modern Claims Platform to Active Directory via HTTPS (OIDC/OAuth 2.0) for SSO
- Modern Claims Platform to Legacy Mainframe via Azure Service Bus and Azure Logic Apps (asynchronous messaging)
- Modern Claims Platform to Notification Service, Payment Gateway, Document Management System, and Audit & Compliance System via HTTPS (REST)

## Technology Stack
- Azure App Service / Azure SPA: Hosts the portal and adjuster workbench for low-overhead cloud deployment.
- Azure Service Bus / Azure Logic Apps: Manages asynchronous decoupling to protect the mainframe batch window (23:00-05:00).
- Anti-Corruption Layer (ACL): Isolates the modern domain model from legacy COBOL/DB2 schemas to absorb quarterly mainframe changes.
- Azure AD / Entra ID with Azure AD Connect: Implements secure SSO with minimal cloud experience.

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates the fragile legacy mainframe behind an Anti-Corruption Layer and asynchronous message bus, satisfying strict change and batch constraints. It decouples modern user experiences from mainframe latency while preserving the 3-year migration path and enabling rapid rollbacks.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a hybrid cloud modernization platform that incrementally replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims system while maintaining legacy processing. It enables online claim submission and modern adjuster workflows via a strangler fig pattern.

## Key Elements
* Azure API Management (API Gateway)
* Azure Static Web Apps (Customer Portal and Adjuster Workspace SPAs, React)
* Azure Container Apps (.NET 8): Claims Core Service, Mainframe Integration Adapter, Audit & Compliance Worker
* Azure Service Bus (Integration Bus/Broker)
* Azure SQL Database (Transactional Store)
* Azure Data Factory with Self-Hosted Integration Runtime (ETL/Data Replication)
* On-Premises COBOL/DB2 Mainframe (Legacy System of Record)
* Azure Active Directory (Identity Provider)

## Relationships
* SPAs -> Azure API Management: HTTPS (OIDC/OAuth2)
* Azure API Management -> Claims Core & Adapter Services: HTTP/2 with propagated JWT bearer tokens
* Claims Core Service <-> Azure Service Bus: AMQP (Asynchronous Messaging)
* Claims Core Service -> Azure SQL Database: TDS (Entity Framework Core)
* Mainframe Integration Adapter -> Legacy Mainframe: IBM MQ / CICS (TCP)
* Azure Data Factory -> On-Premise DB2: JDBC/ODBC via Self-Hosted Integration Runtime (Batch Window: 23:00-05:00)

## Technology Stack
* Azure Container Apps (.NET 8): Provides managed container orchestration for domain microservices, accommodating the team's low cloud experience.
* Azure SQL Database: Delivers ACID-compliant transactional persistence to guarantee zero data loss (R-04).
* Azure Service Bus: Offers managed AMQP messaging to decouple services and ensure reliable asynchronous event processing.
* Azure API Management: Handles native OIDC validation and token propagation without custom identity containers.
* Azure Data Factory: Bridges hybrid networks securely during strict nightly batch windows (23:00-05:00).

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates expensive mainframe interactions behind a dedicated integration adapter and caching layer to meet strict sub-2-second adjuster performance goals. Managed Azure cloud services reduce operational complexity for a team with limited cloud experience while ensuring seamless compliance and fallback capabilities.

## Overview
The system is a hybrid cloud insurance claims modernization platform designed to gradually replace a 30-year-old mainframe while ensuring continuous legacy operation. It provides modern online claim submission and adjuster workflows via secure web applications.

## Key Elements
- Customers and Brokers
- Claims Adjusters
- Customer Portal and Adjuster Workspace SPAs (React, Azure Static Web Apps)
- Azure API Management (Azure API Management)

## Relationships
- Customers and Brokers -> Customer Portal and Adjuster Workspace SPAs: Submit online claims [HTTPS]
- Claims Adjusters -> Customer Portal and Adjuster Workspace SPAs: Manage and process claims [HTTPS]

- Mainframe Integration Adapter <-> Legacy Mainframe: Exchange batch and sync data [SNA / MQ / File Transfer]

## Technology Stack
- Azure Static Web Apps with React: Minimized operational overhead for team with limited cloud experience
- .NET 8 on Azure Container Apps: Robust, scalable backend microservices framework
- Azure SQL Database: Managed relational storage with Entity Framework Core
- Azure Service Bus: Asynchronous, reliable messaging for decoupled claim processing
- Azure API Management: Centralized security, rate limiting, and routing boundary

## Rationale
This hybrid architecture isolates expensive legacy mainframe interactions while enabling independent, cloud-native migration of claim types. It guarantees system consistency and sub-two-second adjuster UI response times despite legacy latency constraints.

Azure API Management.analysis:
## Overview
[A hybrid cloud architecture for Insurance Claims Modernization that gradually migrates claims types from a legacy mainframe to an Azure-hosted modern platform using Azure API Management as the unified gateway. It ensures business continuity and strict system consistency while mitigating the team's limited cloud experience.]

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Customers and Brokers, Claims Adjusters
- **External Systems**: Legacy Mainframe (COBOL/DB2), Active Directory / Azure AD, Notification Service, Payment Gateway, Document Management System, Audit & Compliance System
- **Containers**: Customer Portal & Adjuster Workspace SPAs (React, Azure Static Web Apps), Azure API Management (Azure API Management), Claims Core Service (.NET 8, Azure Container Apps), Mainframe Integration Adapter (.NET 8, Azure Container Apps), Audit & Compliance Worker (.NET 8, Azure Container Apps), Azure Service Bus, Azure SQL Database, Azure Data Factory
- **APIM Components**: JWT Validation Policy, Response Caching Component (Azure Redis Cache), Rate Limiting & Quota Policy, Transformation & Request Routing Policy

## Relationships
- Customer Portal / Adjuster Workspace -> Azure API Management: Send API requests with OIDC/OAuth2 authentication [HTTPS (OIDC/OAuth2)]
- JWT Validation Policy -> Azure Active Directory: Fetch OpenID Connect metadata and JSON Web Keys (JWKS) [HTTPS / OIDC]
- Response Caching Component -> Azure Redis Cache: Cache read-only claim lookup data [TCP / Redis Protocol]
- Transformation & Request Routing Policy -> Claims Core Service: Route modern claim type requests [HTTP/2]
- Transformation & Request Routing Policy -> Mainframe Integration Adapter: Route legacy fallback requests [HTTP/2]
- Azure API Management -> Azure Application Insights: Emit metrics, tracing headers, and logs [HTTPS / OpenTelemetry]

## Technology Stack
- Azure API Management: Unified managed API Gateway reducing operational overhead for cloud-inexperienced teams
- Azure Container Apps & .NET 8: Modern microservices runtime for containerized core services
- Azure SQL Database & Entity Framework Core: Relational data store for modern claim types
- Azure Service Bus: Asynchronous messaging backbone for reliable claim processing
- Azure Static Web Apps & React: Frontend hosting and UI implementation
- Azure Redis Cache: In-memory caching layer to protect the legacy mainframe from performance degradation

## Rationale
[This hybrid architecture decouples the modern web applications from the 30-year-old mainframe via Azure API Management, enabling gradual one-by-one claim type migration without breaking the strict nightly batch window or exceeding expensive mainframe interface limits. By leveraging fully managed Azure services and declarative APIM policies, it minimizes custom infrastructure code to successfully accommodate a team with limited cloud experience.]

Claims Core Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Claims Core Service is a .NET 8 microservice running in Azure Container Apps that processes modern claims while coordinating with a legacy mainframe. It enables gradual claim type migration and rapid rollbacks to meet strict hybrid modernization constraints.

## Key Elements
* Claim Submission Controller (ASP.NET Core Web API)
* Claim Routing Engine (C# Component)
* Claim Domain Model & Engine (C# Class Library)
* Mainframe Anti-Corruption Layer - ACL (C# Component)
* Persistence Repository (EF Core Context)
* Integration Event Publisher/Subscriber (MassTransit .NET)
* Workflow Orchestration Service (C# Component)
* Document Management Client (Typed HttpClient)
* Claim Caching & Read Model Component (Redis / Memory)

## Relationships
* Claim Submission Controller -> Claim Routing Engine: Forwards raw submissions [In-process]
* Claim Routing Engine -> Claim Domain Model & Engine: Routes modernized claim types [In-process]
* Claim Routing Engine -> Mainframe Anti-Corruption Layer: Routes legacy claim types [In-process]
* Claim Domain Model & Engine -> Persistence Repository: Performs transactional reads/writes [TDS via EF Core]
* Claim Domain Model & Engine -> Integration Event Publisher/Subscriber: Publishes domain events [AMQP via Azure Service Bus]
* Workflow Orchestration Service -> Claim Caching & Read Model Component: Updates read models [In-process / Redis]
* Document Management Client -> Document Management System: Uploads and retrieves attachments [HTTPS]
* Mainframe Anti-Corruption Layer -> Mainframe Integration Adapter: Syncs legacy data [gRPC/HTTP]

## Technology Stack
* .NET 8 / C#: Chosen to leverage existing team expertise and minimize the cloud learning curve
* Azure Container Apps: Hosts the microservice with scalable, managed infrastructure
* Entity Framework Core & Azure SQL Database: Provides reliable relational persistence
* MassTransit & Azure Service Bus: Ensures asynchronous, reliable event-driven messaging
* Azure Cache for Redis: Implements CQRS-lite read models to guarantee sub-2-second UI responses

## Rationale
This architecture isolates legacy dependencies through dedicated routing and translation components, allowing seamless claim-by-claim migration and one-day rollbacks. Furthermore, internal caching and decoupled messaging satisfy strict performance and consistency constraints without overwhelming expensive mainframe interfaces.

level: component
scope: "Component diagram for the Claims Core Service container"

Mainframe Integration Adapter.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a hybrid cloud insurance claims modernization platform that gradually replaces a legacy COBOL/DB2 mainframe while maintaining continuous claims processing. It provides online claims submission and adjuster management while ensuring zero data loss and rapid legacy fallback capabilities.

## Key Elements
- Azure API Management (Azure API Management)
- Mainframe Integration Adapter (.NET 8, Azure Container Apps)
- Adapter API Controller (.NET 8 component)
- Mainframe Message Translator with Versioning & Feature Flags (.NET 8 component)
- Outbox Pattern Processor (.NET 8 + Entity Framework Core component)
- Circuit Breaker & Fallback Manager (.NET 8 + Polly component)
- IBM MQ / CICS Client (.NET 8 component)
- On-Premises COBOL/DB2 Mainframe
- Azure Service Bus (Azure Service Bus)

## Relationships
- Azure API Management -> Adapter API Controller: Forward integration requests [HTTP/2]
- Adapter API Controller -> Mainframe Message Translator: Transform payloads [In-Memory]
- Mainframe Message Translator -> Outbox Pattern Processor: Persist transaction state [In-Memory]
- Outbox Pattern Processor -> IBM MQ / CICS Client: Queue dispatch [In-Memory]
- IBM MQ / CICS Client -> Circuit Breaker Manager: Execute legacy calls [TCP/IP via Azure Hybrid Connections]
- Circuit Breaker Manager -> Azure Service Bus: Publish fallback events [AMQP]

## Technology Stack
- .NET 8 on Azure Container Apps: Powers the integration container with modern, maintainable code suited for the team's skillset.
- Entity Framework Core: Manages reliable outbox pattern state persistence to guarantee zero data loss (R-04).
- Polly: Implements circuit breaking and fallback management to handle high mainframe latency (up to 5s).
- IBM MQ / CICS Client via Azure Hybrid Connections: Secures persistent TCP/IP socket communication to the on-premise mainframe.
- Azure Service Bus: Decouples asynchronous messaging and fallback events across the hybrid architecture.

## Rationale
This architecture isolates fragile and expensive-to-change mainframe logic behind a robust, fault-tolerant .NET 8 integration adapter. It satisfies strict hybrid constraints, ensuring transactional consistency and 1-day rollbacks while bridging on-premise systems with Azure.

Audit & Compliance Worker.analysis:
## Overview
The Insurance Claims Modernization system gradually replaces a 30-year-old regional insurer mainframe with a modern hybrid platform. The Audit & Compliance Worker container ensures transactional consistency and regulatory compliance without data loss.

## Key Elements
* Event Consumer Component (.NET 8 Hosted Service / MassTransit)
* Compliance Validator Component (.NET 8)
* Dead Letter Manager Component (.NET 8)
* Audit Repository Access Component (Entity Framework Core)
* Mainframe Sync Component (.NET 8 BackgroundService with native PeriodicTimer)
* External Systems: Azure Service Bus, Azure SQL Database, Azure Blob Storage, Audit & Compliance System

## Relationships
* Event Consumer Component consumes domain events from Azure Service Bus via AMQP.
* Compliance Validator Component evaluates events, routing valid data to Audit Repository Access Component and failures to Dead Letter Manager Component.
* Dead Letter Manager Component stores poisoned messages in Azure Blob Storage.
* Audit Repository Access Component persists compliance logs in Azure SQL Database.
* Mainframe Sync Component pushes compliance packages to the Audit & Compliance System via HTTPS/REST.

## Technology Stack
* .NET 8 / Azure Container Apps: Chosen for core runtime and hosting, leveraging team expertise.
* MassTransit: Simplifies idempotent message processing for consistency (R-04).
* Entity Framework Core: Provides reliable data persistence for Azure SQL Database.
* PeriodicTimer: Implements lightweight scheduling without external orchestrator dependencies.

## Rationale
This component architecture enforces strict consistency and prevents claim loss during migration by combining reliable message consumption with robust dead-lettering and audit logging. The design minimizes cloud complexity, aligning with the team's skillset while satisfying integration constraints.

Azure Service Bus.analysis:
## Overview
[System: Insurance Claims Modernization platform, purpose: Gradually replaces a 30-year-old mainframe claims system with a modern cloud platform while maintaining dual-running and hybrid operations.]

## Key Elements
- Claim Event Topic (`claims-events`): Azure Service Bus Topic for domain events using AMQP.
- Mainframe Sync Queue (`mainframe-sync`): Azure Service Bus Queue utilizing AMQP and Sessions (FIFO) for mainframe order enforcement.
- Duplicate Detection Filter: Native Azure Service Bus property (`RequiresDuplicateDetection`) enforcing exactly-once semantics.
- Subscription Filter Rules (SQL Filters): Broker-level routing rules on topics to segment traffic by claim type.
- DLQ Processor / Forwarder: Auto-forwarding mechanism routing poisoned messages to a triage queue.
- Session State Management: Broker-native session state persistence on the sync queue.

## Relationships
- Claims Core Service -> Claim Event Topic: Publish domain events (`ClaimSubmitted`, `ClaimUpdated`) [AMQP]
- Claim Event Topic -> Subscription Filter Rules: Route events based on claim type [AMQP]
- Mainframe Integration Adapter -> Mainframe Sync Queue: Consume ordered messages and manage session state [AMQP]
- Mainframe Sync Queue -> DLQ Processor: Forward poisoned sync messages [AMQP]

## Technology Stack
- Azure Service Bus: Chosen for managed AMQP messaging, native duplicate detection, and robust partitioning.
- Azure Service Bus Sessions: Utilized for FIFO ordering to prevent race conditions during hybrid DB2 mainframe synchronization.
- Service Bus SQL Filters: Selected for broker-side message routing to support incremental claim-type migration without custom code.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures strict consistency (R-04) and supports gradual, claim-by-claim migration (R-03) while respecting the 3-year hybrid constraint and the team's limited cloud experience. Leveraging broker-native features minimizes custom application code complexity and protects the legacy mainframe interface.

Azure SQL Database.analysis:
## Overview
The Insurance Claims Modernization system gradually replaces a 30-year-old COBOL/DB2 mainframe claims system with a modern hybrid cloud platform. It ensures zero data loss, supports incremental claim type migration, and respects strict legacy batch windows.

## Key Elements
- **Claims Data Model**: Relational tables and schemas structured per claim type using Entity Framework Core Migrations.
- **Data Access Layer**: .NET 8 libraries implementing Repository and Unit of Work patterns.
- **Database Security & Auditing**: Azure SQL Transparent Data Encryption, Row-Level Security, and Audit logs.
- **Temporal Tables**: SQL Server System-Versioning for immutable historical audit trails.
- **Mainframe Sync Staging Tables**: Dedicated schemas for buffering bi-directional state changes.
- **Stored Procedures & Database Triggers**: T-SQL routines for high-performance batch processing and validation.

## Relationships
- **Claims Core Service** -> **Data Access Layer**: In-process method calls [C# / Entity Framework Core]
- **Data Access Layer** -> **Claims Data Model**: Queries and transactions [T-SQL]
- **Azure Data Factory** -> **Mainframe Sync Staging Tables**: Bulk copy operations [Bulk Insert / T-SQL]
- **Mainframe Integration Adapter** -> **Mainframe Sync Staging Tables**: Read/Write sync states [T-SQL via EF Core]
- **Audit & Compliance System** -> **Database Security & Auditing**: Direct log scraping [Azure Monitor / SQL Audit Output]

## Technology Stack
- **Azure SQL Database**: ACID-compliant transactional persistence layer ensuring zero data loss.
- **Entity Framework Core**: ORM for managing relational mappings and LINQ-based data access.
- **T-SQL**: Procedural language used for bulk inserts, triggers, and stored procedures within the batch window.
- **SQL Server System-Versioning**: Built-in temporal tables for automated historical tracking.

## Rationale
This architecture uses hybrid database patterns, staging tables, and temporal versioning to decouple the modern Azure platform from the legacy mainframe. It guarantees strict ACID consistency and rapid rollback capabilities within fixed operational constraints.

[The system modernizes a 30-year-old mainframe insurance claims platform via a hybrid cloud architecture, gradually migrating claim types while maintaining legacy parity. It ensures zero data loss, strict batch compliance, and seamless multi-system integration.]

## Key Elements
* Mainframe Extraction Pipeline (ADF Pipeline)
* Staging Blob Storage (Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2)
* Transformation & Ingestion Flow (ADF Mapping Data Flows)
* Reconciliation & Error-Handling Pipeline (ADF Pipeline)
* Monitoring & Alerting Trigger (ADF Tumbling Window / Azure Monitor)
* Self-Hosted Integration Runtime (SHIR) Cluster (Multi-node active-active)
* Dead-Letter & Quarantine Container (Azure Blob Storage)
* Mainframe Schema Registry (Azure Purview / ADF Dataset Metadata)

## Relationships
* Mainframe Extraction Pipeline reads from On-Premises COBOL/DB2 Mainframe via SHIR Cluster [JDBC / Encrypted TLS over HTTPS]
* Mainframe Extraction Pipeline pushes payloads to Staging Blob Storage [HTTPS]
* Transformation & Ingestion Flow writes to Azure SQL Database [T-SQL/JDBC via Managed Private Endpoint]
* Transformation & Ingestion Flow writes invalid payloads to Dead-Letter & Quarantine Container [REST/HTTPS]
* Transformation & Ingestion Flow reads schema definitions from Mainframe Schema Registry [Metadata API]
* Monitoring & Alerting Trigger invokes Mainframe Extraction Pipeline [Internal ADF Control Plane]
* Mainframe Integration Adapter Container invokes Mainframe Extraction Pipeline [Azure Event Grid / ADF REST API]

## Technology Stack
* Azure Data Factory: Orchestrates ETL, CDC, and batch workflows due to robust hybrid connectivity options
* Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2: Temporarily holds raw parquet files to optimize processing within the strict batch window
* Azure Blob Storage: Provides append blobs for isolating malformed records in the Dead-Letter quarantine
* Azure SQL Database: Stores modern claim data accessed by the Adjuster Workspace via Entity Framework Core
* ADF Self-Hosted Integration Runtime: Secures on-premises mainframe communication without opening inbound firewall ports

## Rationale
[The hybrid architecture utilizes a multi-node SHIR cluster and staging blobs to respect the rigid 6-hour batch window and network boundaries. Automated reconciliation pipelines and idempotency layers guarantee zero data loss and strict consistency without requiring expensive legacy mainframe modifications.]
